:::: {.content-panel .astro-2wc2n45z style="--borderTop: initial;--pageTitleDisplay: block;"}
::: {.sl-container .astro-2wc2n45z style="--borderTop: initial;--pageTitleDisplay: block;"}
# Dual APIs {#_top .astro-np5lzwrf}
:::
::::

::::::::::::::::: {.content-panel .astro-2wc2n45z style="--borderTop: initial;--pageTitleDisplay: block;"}
:::::::::::::::: {.sl-container .astro-2wc2n45z style="--borderTop: initial;--pageTitleDisplay: block;"}
::::::::::::: sl-markdown-content
When you're working with APIs in the Effect ecosystem, you may come
across two different ways to use the same API. These two ways are called
the "data-last" and "data-first" variants.

When an API supports both variants, we call them "dual" APIs.

Here's an illustration of these two variants using
`Effect.map`{dir="auto"}.

::: {.autolink-heading-container .level-h2 tabindex="-1"}
## Effect.map as a dual API {#effectmap-as-a-dual-api}

[[![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)]{.anchor-icon
aria-hidden="true"}](index.html#effectmap-as-a-dual-api){.anchor-link
aria-labelledby="effectmap-as-a-dual-api"}
:::

The `Effect.map`{dir="auto"} function is defined with two TypeScript
overloads. The terms "data-last" and "data-first" refer to the position
of the `self`{dir="auto"} argument (also known as the "data") in the
signatures of the two overloads:

::: expressive-code
<figure class="frame not-content">
<pre data-language="ts"><code>declare const map: {  //                               ┌─── data-last  //                               ▼  &lt;A, B&gt;(f: (a: A) =&gt; B): &lt;E, R&gt;(self: Effect&lt;A, E, R&gt;) =&gt; Effect&lt;B, E, R&gt;  //             ┌─── data-first  //             ▼  &lt;A, E, R, B&gt;(self: Effect&lt;A, E, R&gt;, f: (a: A) =&gt; B): Effect&lt;B, E, R&gt;}</code></pre>
<div class="copy">
<div>

</div>
</div>
</figure>
:::

::: {.autolink-heading-container .level-h3 tabindex="-1"}
### data-last

[[![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)]{.anchor-icon
aria-hidden="true"}](index.html#data-last){.anchor-link
aria-labelledby="data-last"}
:::

In the first overload, the `self`{dir="auto"} argument comes **last**:

::: expressive-code
<figure class="frame not-content">
<pre data-language="ts"><code>declare const map: &lt;A, B&gt;(  f: (a: A) =&gt; B) =&gt; &lt;E, R&gt;(self: Effect&lt;A, E, R&gt;) =&gt; Effect&lt;B, E, R&gt;</code></pre>
<div class="copy">
<div>

</div>
</div>
</figure>
:::

This version is commonly used with the `pipe`{dir="auto"} function. You
start by passing the `Effect`{dir="auto"} as the initial argument to
`pipe`{dir="auto"} and then chain transformations like
`Effect.map`{dir="auto"}:

**Example** (Using data-last with `pipe`{dir="auto"})

::: expressive-code
<figure class="frame not-content">
<pre data-language="ts"><code>const mappedEffect = pipe(effect, Effect.map(func))</code></pre>
<div class="copy">
<div>

</div>
</div>
</figure>
:::

This style is helpful when chaining multiple transformations, making the
code easier to follow in a pipeline format:

::: expressive-code
<figure class="frame not-content">
<pre data-language="ts"><code>pipe(effect, Effect.map(func1), Effect.map(func2), ...)</code></pre>
<div class="copy">
<div>

</div>
</div>
</figure>
:::

::: {.autolink-heading-container .level-h3 tabindex="-1"}
### data-first

[[![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)]{.anchor-icon
aria-hidden="true"}](index.html#data-first){.anchor-link
aria-labelledby="data-first"}
:::

In the second overload, the `self`{dir="auto"} argument comes **first**:

::: expressive-code
<figure class="frame not-content">
<pre data-language="ts"><code>declare const map: &lt;A, E, R, B&gt;(  self: Effect&lt;A, E, R&gt;,  f: (a: A) =&gt; B) =&gt; Effect&lt;B, E, R&gt;</code></pre>
<div class="copy">
<div>

</div>
</div>
</figure>
:::

This form doesn't require `pipe`{dir="auto"}. Instead, you provide the
`Effect`{dir="auto"} directly as the first argument:

**Example** (Using data-first without `pipe`{dir="auto"})

::: expressive-code
<figure class="frame not-content">
<pre data-language="ts"><code>const mappedEffect = Effect.map(effect, func)</code></pre>
<div class="copy">
<div>

</div>
</div>
</figure>
:::

This version works well when you only need to perform a single operation
on the `Effect`{dir="auto"}.

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,){.starlight-aside__icon
.astro-4rgy7crp} Choosing Between Styles

::: starlight-aside__content
Both overloads achieve the same result. Choose the one that best suits
your coding style and enhances readability for your team.
:::
